items.title: Asymptotic linearity implies asymptotic normality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be iid with law $P$, let $k<\infty$, and let $\widehat\psi_n$ estimate $\psi(P)\in\mathbb R^k$. If it is asymptotically linear at $P$ with influence function $\varphi\in L^2_0(P)^k$, then

$$\sqrt n\{\widehat\psi_n-\psi(P)\}\Rightarrow N_k(0,\Sigma_\varphi),\qquad \Sigma_\varphi=P[\varphi\varphi^T].$$

The covariance may be singular. This is a distributional limit only; the theorem asserts neither local regularity nor estimator attainment of an efficiency bound.

items.title: Finite-dimensional LAN convolution bound for differentiable functionals
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $d,k\ge1$ be finite. Let $\{P_{n,h}:h\in\mathbb R^d\}$ be LAN at $h=0$ with positive-definite information matrix $K$ and central sequence $\Delta_n$. Let $\psi_{n,h}\in\mathbb R^k$ be a local target such that for every fixed $h$,

$$\delta_n(h):=\sqrt n(\psi_{n,h}-\psi_{n,0})\longrightarrow Dh$$

for a fixed matrix $D\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}$. Suppose $T_n=\sqrt n(\widehat\psi_n-\psi_{n,0})$ is regular for this target: under each fixed $P_{n,h}$, $T_n-\delta_n(h)\Rightarrow W$ for the same Borel law $W$. Then there is a probability law $\nu$ on $\mathbb R^k$ such that

$$\mathcal L(W)=N_k(0,DK^{-1}D^T)*\nu.$$

The Gaussian covariance may be singular. No finite-moment hypothesis on $W$ or $\nu$ is needed.

items.title: A one-sided DQM path yields an iid LAN proxy
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $t\mapsto P_t$ be a one-sided path ($0\le t<\epsilon$) of probability laws on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ dominated by one supplied sigma-finite measure $\mu$, with supplied densities $p_t$ and $P_0=P$. Suppose the path is differentiable in quadratic mean at $0$ with score $s\in L^2(P)$, in the sense of [[def-dqm-submodel-through-a-law]]. Put $I=P[s^2]$. For a fixed $h\ge0$, let $t_n=h/\sqrt n$ and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid $P$. On $S=\{p_0>0\}$ set $\alpha_t=P_t(S^c)$ and, for sufficiently small $t$, define

$$q_t(x)=\frac{\mathbf1_S(x)p_t(x)}{(1-\alpha_t)p_0(x)}\quad\text{on }S,\qquad q_t(x)=0\quad\text{on }S^c.$$

Then $q_t$ is a probability density relative to $P$. With $L_n=\prod_{i=1}^nq_{t_n}(X_i)$ and $\Delta_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^ns(X_i)$,

$$\left\|P_{t_n}^{\otimes n}-L_nP^{\otimes n}\right\|_{\rm TV}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \log L_n=h\Delta_n-\tfrac12h^2I+o_P(1),\qquad \Delta_n\Rightarrow N(0,I).$$

For $h=0$ take $L_n=1$ and use the convention $\log0=-\infty$. The proxy $L_nP^{\otimes n}$ is the normalized absolutely continuous component; the conclusion does not assert a full likelihood ratio for $P_{t_n}^{\otimes n}$.

items.title: Semiparametric information bound for regular asymptotically linear estimators
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $P$ be a law in a statistical model, let $\mathcal T\subseteq L^2_0(P)$ be its closed score tangent space, and let $\psi$ be a pathwise differentiable $\mathbb R^k$-valued functional with canonical gradient $\phi_{\rm can}\in\mathcal T^k$. Write $V_{\rm can}=P[\phi_{\rm can}\phi_{\rm can}^T]$. Let $\widehat\psi_n$ be asymptotically linear at $P$ with influence function $\varphi\in L^2_0(P)^k$. Assume that for every allowed one-sided DQM path $P_t$ with score $s$ and every fixed $h\ge0$, under $P_{h/\sqrt n}^{\otimes n}$ the centered estimator $\sqrt n\{\widehat\psi_n-\psi(P_{h/\sqrt n})\}$ converges to one law independent of $h$, equal to its limit at $h=0$. Then $\varphi$ represents the pathwise derivative on $\mathcal T$, so

$$\varphi\in\phi_{\rm can}+(\mathcal T^\perp)^k,\qquad P[\varphi\varphi^T]-V_{\rm can}=P[(\varphi-\phi_{\rm can})(\varphi-\phi_{\rm can})^T]\succeq0.$$

By [[thm-asymptotic-linearity-implies-normality]], this is the covariance lower bound for the estimator's asymptotic normal limit. The theorem does not assert that an estimator attaining the bound exists.

items.title: Convolution bound for general regular estimators
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $\psi$ be pathwise differentiable at $P$ with tangent space $\mathcal T$ and canonical gradient $\phi_{\rm can}\in\mathcal T^k$, and write $V_{\rm can}=P[\phi_{\rm can}\phi_{\rm can}^T]$. If $\mathcal T\ne\{0\}$, suppose a directed family of finite-dimensional, dominated QMD models $\{P_{\gamma,\theta}:\theta\in\Theta_\gamma\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_\gamma}\}$, with each $\Theta_\gamma$ open and $P_{\gamma,\theta_{\gamma,0}}=P$, has score spans $\mathcal S_\gamma\subseteq\mathcal T$ whose union is dense in $\mathcal T$. In each model let $S_\gamma\in L^2_0(P)^{d_\gamma}$ be a score basis, let $I_\gamma=P[S_\gamma S_\gamma^T]$ be nonsingular, and let $D_\gamma=P[\phi_{\rm can}S_\gamma^T]$. Assume for each fixed $h\in\mathbb R^{d_\gamma}$ that $\sqrt n\{\psi(P_{\gamma,\theta_{\gamma,0}+h/\sqrt n})-\psi(P)\}\to D_\gamma h$, and that under each local law the centered estimator $\sqrt n\{\widehat\psi_n-\psi(P_{\gamma,\theta_{\gamma,0}+h/\sqrt n})\}$ converges to one common law $L$, independent of $\gamma$ and $h$. Suppose $L$ has finite covariance. By [[thm-qmd-implies-lan-for-iid]], each model has the required LAN proxy; [[lem-finite-dimensional-functional-convolution-bound]] then applies with derivative matrix $D_\gamma$. If $\mathcal T=\{0\}$, no submodel family is needed. Then

$$\operatorname{Cov}(L)\succeq V_{\rm can}.$$

This is a lower bound for general regular estimators; asymptotic linearity is not assumed.

items.title: A finite-mean functional without a square-integrable influence curve
items.statement: Every finite-mean law has a finite-variance influence curve for its mean functional in the dominated local model generated by bounded mean-zero score tilts.

items.title: The sample mean attains the unrestricted mean bound
items.statement: Let $P$ be any law on $\mathbb R$ with $P[X^2]<\infty$, let $\mu=PX$, and consider the local model whose allowed paths are all bounded mean-zero tilts $dP_{t,s}=(1+ts)dP$ for sufficiently small $t\ge0$. For $\psi(Q)=QX$, the sample mean $\bar X_n$ is regular along each allowed one-sided path (the centered root-$n$ error has one common limit law for every fixed $h\ge0$), and is asymptotically linear with influence function $X-\mu$. Its asymptotic variance equals the unrestricted mean bound.
